text:
Two minutes in and I hate it. Rant incoming!
I really hope ING is taking the terrible star ratings of this new app seriously. I’ve used it for about TWO MINUTES and I’ve already come across multiple issues and I’m sure I’ll find more as I’m forced to use it.

Firstly, when transferring money, the app is now hell-bent on you getting the recipient’s account name precise. This was never an issue for me in the old app. If I had the correct BSB and account number, I could make the transfer without fighting with the app over exactly how someone’s account name is formatted.

Secondly, what on earth happened to sharing bank details? Previously, when I copied my account details, ING gave me a simple, nicely formatted message:

“My ING account details are:
BSB: ******
ACC: *********”

Now when I copy my details, I get my BSB and account number MASHED TOGETHER into one giant line of numbers with no labels or formatting whatsoever. Who thought that was an improvement? The entire purpose of copying bank details is to make them easy to share accurately.

Did you actually test this app  before launching it and forcing your existing customers to switch?

There’s an old saying: WHY FIX WHAT AIN’T BROKE?

The old ING app was simple, intuitive and functional. That simplicity was part of what made ING good. This new app feels like someone redesigned things for the sake of redesigning them without a thought about user experience. 

And please, for the love of God, stop replacing perfectly functional features with things that feel like they were designed by AI without anyone checking whether the end result makes any sense.

This is dumb, sloppy work. You’re going to lose loyal customers who were loyal precisely because ING felt smarter and simpler than the alternatives.

Do better, ING. Fix it.

text:
Not a net improvement. The new ING app is not a nett improvement on the old one. 

Please bring back the quick view balances without logging in. This system where you have to hide your balances with a long 2-finger press before logging out is just plain bad security. If you forget to do it, your balances are there to be seen next time you log in. 

I also don’t like that the app just logs you in immediately if you have face recognition turned on  - if you tap on the app by accident, suddenly you are logged into your bank. Again, this is not good for privacy and security. There should be a login button. 

I generally feel that you were trying to be too clever when developing the app, and as a result have tried to save clicks/taps on the wrong things. 
I would recommend looking at the Westpac and Macquarie apps to get ideas for improvements. One excellent feature that Westpac has introduced is the ability to fill out the description for the transaction by selecting a previous description which matches the transaction you are making. This a genuine pleasure - convenient, quick, and even helps with security when making common types of payments because if you don’t see the expected description, it’s a flag that you might have selected the wrong beneficiary. 

The new app has bugs, such as option buttons that don’t work - for example, if you click on Change to change your account name under Manage Account, it doesn’t work. (I did find how to do this by an alternative method in settings, but why have a Change button if it is not functional?). 

Generally, the new app is clunky and needs a lot of work to get it to the level I’d expect. I use apps from most of the major banks, and ING needs to catch up. There are no innovative new features or capabilities to offset these inconvenient issues.

Style over substance. Old app is better simply because it is more functional. Nice to have notifications - I now know when my pay hits my account. But many very basic functions that the old app had (for example, and as other reviews have mentioned, the running balance that the old app displays next to each transaction) are sorely missed. The ability to view account balances without having to log in is gone. Scheduled payments are no longer displayed according to the date of the next scheduled payment - they are now displayed according to the date when the payment was first scheduled. As someone who relies on scheduled payments from their ING accounts for their fortnightly budgeting, this is incredibly frustrating and inconvenient - I need to be able to see when scheduled payments are due to take place next; the past date on which I first scheduled the payment is pretty irrelevant to me. text:
Major update worsened user experience considerably but probably making ING heaps more money…. Several months back when this new app was released, users of the old app noted some features were missing. A big one was the running total, which made it really easy to keep tabs on whether your balance was trending up or down month to month. When this feature disappeared I just assumed it was an oversight. I submitted feedback about it as I’m sure many others have, and I assumed they’d probably add it back in before too long.

Months on, after no change to the app, I’ve realised the change was most likely deliberate: one of the conditions for receiving bonus interest for the month is that your savings account balance has increased. Not providing a running total means that keeping track of this (so that action can be taken to ensure the balance increases) now requires deliberate attention on the part of the user.

At the time of writing, a user not realising that they need to defer some spending to hit this particular target means that ING gets to pay them 0.01% interest instead of 5.5% interest for that month.

This seems like a really scummy, anti-consumer change, especially for people with ADHD, who may struggle to do this kind of admin even if they’re aware of the issue.

text:
Whatever you do don’t upgrade to the new app. As a grown adult well capable of making my own financial decisions there is nothing worse than being bossed around like a recalcitrant toddler by my bank. I use banks for same reasons as anyone else, no one pays in cash anymore as we’ve left every part of the 1900’s far behind but there’s also the convenience of being able to access your money without the security risk carrying it all with you all of the time. I recognise ING terms and conditions don’t allow for logging into other peoples profiles but ING also doesn’t allow you to get multiple debit cards on your own account, doesn’t allow more than two debit card accounts under your name and doesn’t do bank accounts for kids under 18. The old app had ways of getting around some of these problems, once my oldest hit 18 we sorted our banking so his younger sisters took the second debit card account under our names, I put my card on their phones, my son and I just logged into each others accounts as needed and while not perfect it was close enough and we lived our lives. 

The new app which doesn’t allow for logging out of your own profile and logging into another one has made things incredibly difficult requiring us to be on the phone discussing what’s needed so funds can transfer and things can get paid with one time SMS authorisations and ensuring the correct balance is in the correct account at the correct time. It’s so much simpler when one person can log in, check balances and fix whatever needs fixing. The app developers aren’t low income families struggling to pay the bills and it really shows with this doubling down of already overly restrictive infantilising of people who are also expected to financially support themselves and others, vote, drink alcohol and operate heavy machinery. I can do all that but I can’t dictate who can access my money and how. 

All the things I loved about ING are slowly and silently being dropped, the time I managed to get into arrears (genuinely through no deliberate fault of my own) and ING gave me an advance on my regular income so I could buy groceries for the two days my accounts were in such a mess? I bet you wouldn’t do that today. I had to dispute a visa transaction recently, in less than 24 hours of the purchase and being told you’ll attempt to get some of my money back but it will take 30-60 business days? We live in a time where everything is instant and you expect me to believe the banking industry is somehow unable to make things move quickly? Rubbish. Utter rubbish. The delay only serves the banks just as this new app does, it has nothing to do with the customer so stop trying to sell it to us as beneficial, why pretend when we all know the truth?

I note many users complain they can’t share the BSB and Account number together so they’re forced to do so separately yet I have the opposite issue? In the new app I can only share the BSB and Account number together when I want to share them separately as oftentimes in online forms these are seperate boxes and I’ve memorised the BSB so I only need the account number. Another review noted other banks having pie charts and savings goals, I’m off to see which bank that is because a user friendly app with features to make managing my money easier without unnecessary restrictions sounds very attractive right now.

the new app which doesn’t allow for logging out of your own profile and logging into another one has made things incredibly difficult requiring us to be on the phone discussing what’s needed so funds can transfer and things can get paid with one time sms authorisations and ensuring the correct balance is in the correct account at the correct time. it’s so much simpler when one person can log in, check balances and fix whatever needs fixing. the app developers aren’t low income families struggling to pay the bills and it really shows with this doubling down of already overly restrictive infantilising of people who are also expected to financially support themselves and others, vote, drink alcohol and operate heavy machinery. i can do all that but i can’t dictate who can access my money and how. 

all the things i loved about ing are slowly and silently being dropped, the time i managed to get into arrears (genuinely through no deliberate fault of my own) and ing gave me an advance on my regular income so i could buy groceries for the two days my accounts were in such a mess? i bet you wouldn’t do that today. i had to dispute a visa transaction recently, in less than 24 hours of the purchase and being told you’ll attempt to get some of my money back but it will take 30-60 business days? we live in a time where everything is instant and you expect me to believe the banking industry is somehow unable to make things move quickly? rubbish. utter rubbish. the delay only serves the banks just as this new app does, it has nothing to do with the customer so stop trying to sell it to us as beneficial, why pretend when we all know the truth?

i note many users complain they can’t share the bsb and account number together so they’re forced to do so separately yet i have the opposite issue? in the new app i can only share the bsb and account number together when i want to share them separately as oftentimes in online forms these are seperate boxes and i’ve memorised the bsb so i only need the account number. another review noted other banks having pie charts and savings goals, i’m off to see which bank that is because a user friendly app with features to make managing my money easier without unnecessary restrictions sounds very attractive right now.

text:
Very disappointed. I was forced to switch to the new ING app, and it’s one of the most frustrating banking app updates I’ve experienced. The previous app was simple, intuitive, and made managing my finances quick and easy. This redesign has done the exact opposite.

Previously, I had my accounts organised exactly how I wanted them, making it easy to distinguish between my everyday accounts, long-term savings, and credit card. The new app has removed that clarity, and it’s now difficult to quickly identify which account is which.

The biggest issue is the loss of easy access to my credit card. I used to be able to check my balance and transactions at a glance throughout the day, but that functionality now appears to be buried or missing altogether.

Another major frustration is that my partner and I could previously use the same phone and simply switch between our individual ING accounts. That feature has been removed, making the app far less practical for our household.

This update feels like a redesign for the sake of redesign, rather than an improvement to the user experience. Core functionality has been made more complicated, navigation is less intuitive, and tasks that were once quick now take far more effort.

I’ve banked with ING for years because of its excellent digital experience, but this update has seriously undermined that. Unless these issues are addressed, I’ll be looking at moving my banking elsewhere. I genuinely hope ING listens to the overwhelming customer feedback and prioritises usability over aesthetics.
